also notable for their contents in vitamin C. Fruits that provide vitamin C include acerola (Malpighia emarginata), also called cherry
of the Antilles: It is an acid fruit of red color (there are other varieties of yellow and purple colors), which is characterized by con-
taining a quantity of vitamin C of 690–4800 mg/100 g. It can be eaten fresh, although its main consumption is as juice. It is also
used in the food industry for vitamin C enrichment of fruit juices. The folic acid content of fruits is low, although in oranges it is
40 mg/100 g; it is 45–62 mg/100 g in strawberries and raspberries; and it is 30 mg/100 g in kiwi (Table 2). The vitamin A intake from
fruits comes from carotenoids (a-carotene, b-carotene, g-carotene, and b-cryptoxanthin), which are the ones that can become
retinol inside the organism.
